results.title: Cloud GPU: on-demand, reserved and spot, and why neoclouds change the board (with 2026 prices) | lo0 — Tech Blog
highlights:
## TL;DR

An H100 SXM5 on-demand costs between 2.49 USD/GPU-hour (Lambda, a neocloud) and 12.29 USD/GPU-hour (Azure ND H100 v5) depending on the provider, a spread of 5× between the neocloud floor and the hyperscaler ceiling. The reserved mode (a 1-3 year commitment) lowers the price by 20-40 % and is the number comparable to amortising your own iron; the spot/preemptible mode takes another 40-65 % off, but with a risk of interruption on less than 2 minutes’ notice. For the on-prem vs cloud analysis of this series (article sovereign on-premise vs hyperscalers), neocloud reserved is the correct reference: at 1.49-2.10 USD/GPU-hour with a 3-year commitment, neoclouds compete head-on with the TCO of your own iron at medium utilisation.

...

### On-demand

Pay per use with no commitment, billed by the hour or by the minute. Maximum flexibility; maximum price. Applies to: development, experimentation, occasional capacity peaks and any workload whose lifetime is unpredictable. The absence of commitment has a cost: the on-demand premium over reserved ranges from 25 % to 60 % depending on the provider.

### Reserved / committed

A 1 or 3 year contract that guarantees capacity in exchange for a discount on the on-demand rate. At hyperscalers it goes by the name Reserved Instance (AWS), Committed Use Discount (GCP) or Azure Reservation. At neoclouds it is negotiated directly and can include the choice of node, network (Ethernet or InfiniBand) and region. Typical discounts:

| Term | Discount on on-demand (market reference) |
| --- | --- |
| 1 year | 20-37 % |
| 3 years | 30-45 % |

Reserved is the model comparable to on-prem: in both cases a fixed cost is incurred up front (amortised capex on-prem; committed payment in the cloud). The formula for the effective cost per GPU-hour is the same in both cases:

$$\text{cost/GPU-hour}_{reserved} = \frac{\text{committed price (USD/GPU-h)} \times 8760}{\text{contracted hours}}$$

...

### Spot / preemptible

Idle provider capacity offered at a 40-65 % discount on on-demand, on the condition that it can be reclaimed with 30 seconds to 2 minutes of notice (AWS Spot, GCP Spot VMs). The discount is real and reproducible; so is the interruption risk.

...

Neoclouds (or GPU-specialised clouds) are infrastructure providers focused exclusively on GPU compute for AI workloads, without the diversity of services of the hyperscalers. SemiAnalysis coined the term in 2024 and identifies CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe at the top tier (SemiAnalysis, 2024).

Structural differences with respect to the hyperscalers:

| Dimension | Neoclouds (CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius…) | Hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 on-demand price | 2.49-6.16 USD/GPU-hour | 6.88-12.29 USD/GPU-hour |
| Interconnect network | InfiniBand NDR 400 Gbps (CoreWeave, Voltage Park), Ethernet 200+ Gbps (Lambda, Nebius) | Proprietary Ethernet (EFA, GVNIC) or InfiniBand (only p5/H100 on AWS) |
| Access to new hardware | NVIDIA priority access (CoreWeave is an NVIDIA shareholder); H200/B200 catalogue available earlier | Slower catalogue; B200 in reserved or limited capacity in 2026 |
| Contracts | 1-36 months, negotiated directly | Standard RI (1-3 years), no node negotiation |
| Additional services | Managed Kubernetes, storage, bare-metal | Complete ecosystem (IAM, VPC, databases, ML services…) |
| Egress | Zero-egress or flat fee (Lambda, Voltage Park, Nebius) | 0.08-0.12 USD/GB (AWS, GCP, Azure) |
| Sovereignty | Varies: Nebius (EU), Crusoe (US, clean), CoreWeave (US/EU) | US CLOUD Act; no guarantee of EU jurisdiction |

...

| Voltage Park | H100 | Ethernet (1.99 USD) / InfiniBand 3200 Gbps (2.49 USD) | US | Merged with Lightning AI in Jan. 2026; no minimums; non-profit Navigation Fund |
| Together AI | H100, A100 | Ethernet | US | Inference platform + raw compute |
| GMI Cloud | H100, H200 | Ethernet | Asia/US | H200 on-demand from 2.60 USD/hr |

The key reading: at high utilisation, on-prem TCO (~2.83 USD/GPU-hour all-in according to Spheron, 2026) competes with the 3-year reserved of the neocloud (~1.49-2.97 USD/GPU-hour). On-prem wins at high utilisation when the all-in cost drops below 2.5 USD; neocloud reserved wins when utilisation is medium or low, because it does not pay for idle capex. Spot lowers the cloud floor but is not comparable: interruption makes it incompatible with continuous serving, which is the case where on-prem competes.

| Neocloud 3-yr reserved | low (1.5-2.1 USD/GPU-h) | low, financial commitment | depends on the provider | comparable to amortised on-prem; very stable base load |
| Neocloud spot | minimum (1-2.5 USD/GPU-h) | high (interruption <2 min) | depends on the provider | batch, fine-tuning with checkpoints, hyperparameter search |
| Hyperscaler on-demand | high (6.9-12.3 USD/GPU-h) | low | NO (CLOUD Act) | integration with AWS/GCP/Azure services; no alternative |
| Hyperscaler reserved | medium-high (3-9 USD/GPU-h) | low | NO (CLOUD Act) | lock-in to the hyperscaler ecosystem is justified |
| Hyperscaler spot | medium (1.1-3.7 USD/GPU-h) | high (interruption) | NO (CLOUD Act) | batch with no sovereignty requirement; more availability than neocloud spot |
| Amortised on-prem (>70 % util.) | low (~2.3-2.8 USD/GPU-h all-in) | low (no interruption) | total (your own hardware) | stable, high base load; maximum sovereignty |

On-prem competes with neocloud 3-yr reserved when utilisation exceeds 65-70 % (see GPU utilisation as FinOps).

results.title: I met Zachary Gulsby (fantastic fella), partnerships lead Runpod, at DevWeek in New York last week — so I asked him what actually changes for founders in 2026. | Saad Durrani
highlights:
His prediction: as Blackwell and the B300 chips come down in price, the compute that used to be locked behind big-lab budgets opens up to everyone else. Founders who couldn't afford to run powerful models suddenly can.

The numbers already back him up. B300 cloud time has dropped to ~$2.45 per GPU-hour on spot. Inference is down to ~$0.24 per million tokens — roughly 35x cheaper per token than the generation it replaced. (SemiAnalysis, April 2026.)

results.title: Citi: AI Inference Bottleneck Shifts From Chips to Power and Data Centers, A100 GPUs Up 11% in Six Weeks | Gate News
highlights: According to Citi analysts, AI inference demand remains strong with the bottleneck shifting from advanced chips to older-generation GPUs and power infrastructure, the bank said on June 16 based on a report released June 14. A100 GPU rental prices rose 11% over six weeks, indicating sustained demand beyond cutting-edge hardware. The bank noted that data center capacity constraints now pose a major challenge: one private neocloud operator has signed for 4.9 GW of demand but has over 40 GW planned in its pipeline. Data center site selection increasingly depends on power costs around 9-12 cents per kilowatt-hour, renewable energy availability, and long-term power purchase agreements. Citi said AI infrastructure costs will continue rising as capital expenditures for equipment, power access, and early-stage infrastructure investments increase.

results.title: Most teams pick a GPU on specs. The market prices it on scarcity. | Mercatus AI | The Open Intelligence Exchange
highlights:
Most teams pick a GPU on specs. The market prices it on scarcity.

Here's where on-demand rental sits across the NVIDIA data center stack right now:

A100 80GB: $2.04/hr
H100: $3.62/hr
H200: $4.37/hr
B200: $5.95/hr
B300: $8.43/hr

A B300-hour runs about 4x an A100-hour. Same vendor, same on-demand model, four years of architecture priced into one ladder.

The part worth watching: nearly every rung moved up 6 to 13% in the last 30 days. Newer silicon isn't just more expensive, it's inflating faster than the hardware it replaces.

So the real question isn't which GPU is fastest. It's whether the throughput on the top rung actually clears the rent.

results.title: 海外云服务商全线涨价，国内 GPU 租赁迎来进口替代窗口期|算力|运营|gpu_网易订阅
highlights:
一、行业现状：海外头部云服务商同步上调算力相关服务价格

2026 年上半年，全球主流海外云厂商完成多轮算力、网络传输服务调价，打破云计算行业长期低价竞争的运行惯例。亚马逊 AWS 在 1 月上调机器学习专用 GPU 实例定价，面向大模型训练的 P5 系列高端算力统一提价 15%，8 卡 H200 实例单小时租金由 34.61 美元上涨至 39.80 美元，北美区域溢价幅度更高。谷歌云 5 月启动全球数据传输调价，北美地区单位 GB 传输费用涨幅 100%，欧洲、亚洲区域同步上调 40% 至 42%，推理业务跨区域流量成本直接翻倍。欧洲区域云服务商同步跟进，Hetzner 全线云服务器涨幅 30%-38%，OVHcloud 分阶段上调 5%-10% 算力服务报价36氪。

本轮涨价由三层刚性成本驱动。第一，全球高端 GPU 硬件供需缺口持续扩大，H100、H200 交付周期拉长至 12 至 18 个月，硬件采购成本持续上行；第二，海外数据中心电力、液冷运维成本逐年抬升；第三，海外云厂商经营策略转向盈利优先，结束长期低价换份额的运营模式。国内企业跨境租用海外算力的综合成本出现显著抬升，除硬件租金上涨外，跨境数据传输、合规备案、汇率波动叠加，整体综合使用成本较 2024 年同期提升 42%。国内中小 AI 创业公司、垂直行业数字化企业逐步缩减海外算力采购预算，需求持续向本土 GPU 租赁市场转移。

...

2.2 综合使用成本形成价差优势，本土算力 TCO 低于跨境方案

抛开跨境传输、合规附加支出，本土 GPU 租赁单卡月度综合成本较海外同规格实例低 25%-35%。国内算力机房集中布局清洁能源配套区域，电力成本低于欧美数据中心；本土服务商无需叠加国际带宽溢价，中小型推理、模型微调业务的单位 Token 算力成本优势进一步放大。中国信通院监测数据显示，2026 年一季度国内算力租赁市场规模 680 亿元，同比增长 62%，其中因海外涨价回流的本土订单增量占新增市场份额 37%，企业客户回流覆盖通用推理、垂直模型训练、多媒体渲染全场景。

...

四、行业发展结论：进口替代窗口期具备中长期持续性

海外云服务商全线涨价并非短期阶段性调整，硬件供给约束、能源成本上行、厂商盈利诉求三重因素将长期推高跨境算力使用成本，国内 GPU 租赁进口替代窗口期至少持续 2 至 3 年。短期市场呈现需求快速回流特征，具备全域调度、异构算力兼容能力的本土算力服务商将优先抢占增量市场；仅依靠单一机房、无调度技术的小型集群，受利用率限制难以承接大规模回流订单，市场份额将持续向标准化运营平台集中。中长期维度，国产 AI 芯片生态持续完善叠加本土算力调度技术迭代，本土 GPU 租赁服务将逐步覆盖训练、推理全场景需求，海外算力仅作为特殊场景补充。行业发展主线从跨境算力采购转向自主可控本土算力租赁，依托存量调度盘活基础设施资源，抓住进口替代周期完成行业高质量发展转型。

results.title: Paperspace vs CoreWeave: Cost, Control, and Enterprise AI Fit-OneSource Cloud
highlights:
### Paperspace (DigitalOcean)

Paperspace provides GPU cloud instances — called GPU Droplets since its acquisition by DigitalOcean — with a focus on developer accessibility and straightforward pricing. The platform offers GPU instances ranging from single-GPU development environments to multi-GPU configurations, with transparent per-hour pricing and no hidden bandwidth charges.

...

### CoreWeave

CoreWeave is an AI-native cloud provider that built its platform specifically for GPU-intensive workloads. It offers large-scale GPU clusters — including NVIDIA H100 and GB200 architecture — with pricing that has been reported to be 30-60% lower than equivalent configurations on hyperscale cloud providers.

CoreWeave targets organizations running large-scale AI training, inference at scale, and GPU-intensive compute workloads. The platform provides Kubernetes-based orchestration, high-performance networking with InfiniBand, and the ability to provision multi-node GPU clusters for distributed training. CoreWeave became the first provider to receive NVIDIA's GB200 "Exemplar Cloud" designation, reflecting its close partnership with NVIDIA.

...

### Pricing and Cost Model

Paperspace offers transparent, per-hour GPU pricing with no egress or bandwidth surcharges — a differentiator compared to hyperscale cloud providers where data transfer costs compound. Pricing is straightforward and predictable for individual instances, making it easy for developers and small teams to estimate costs.

CoreWeave offers lower per-GPU-hour pricing than hyperscale cloud providers, with a pricing structure designed for large-scale, sustained GPU usage. CoreWeave has also introduced flexible pricing models for inference workloads that experience demand fluctuations. However, pricing for the largest configurations and longest commitments may require contract negotiation.

Comparison: Paperspace provides simplicity and transparency for smaller-scale usage. CoreWeave provides lower unit economics for large-scale, sustained GPU workloads. Neither provides the reserved-capacity, predictable-monthly-cost model that dedicated private infrastructure offers — both are usage-based, meaning costs scale with consumption.

Comparing only per-GPU-hour pricing. The per-GPU rate is one component of total cost. Data transfer charges, storage costs, networking fees, and the internal engineering cost of managing the environment all contribute to the total cost of AI infrastructure. Evaluating providers on GPU rate alone produces an incomplete picture.
